job_statement: When I need to implement CI/CD for my application, I want to understand what OpenShift Pipelines capabilities are available, so I can determine if it meets my automation requirements
related_jobs: Understand pipeline concepts; Evaluate CI/CD tooling options
desired_outcomes: Minimize time spent researching CI/CD platform capabilities; Minimize uncertainty about platform fit for microservices architecture; Maximize confidence in platform selection decision
notes: This is a foundational learning job that precedes implementation. The section lists serverless, decentralized team support, integration with OCP tools, and Developer console management as key differentiators.

job_statement: When I need to build container images in my CI/CD pipeline, I want to know what build tools are supported, so I can choose the right image building strategy for my project
parent_job: When I need to implement CI/CD for my application, I want to understand what OpenShift Pipelines capabilities are available, so I can determine if it meets my automation requirements
desired_outcomes: Minimize time spent finding supported image build tools; Maximize portability of image builds across OpenShift platforms; Minimize risk of choosing an incompatible build tool
notes: Specific to understanding build tool options (S2I, Buildah, Buildpacks, Kaniko). This is implementation-specific knowledge supporting the main job of evaluating platform capabilities.

job_statement: When I am designing a CI/CD workflow, I want to understand how to structure reusable units of work, so I can create maintainable and composable pipeline components
related_jobs: Design pipeline orchestration; Share data between pipeline steps
desired_outcomes: Minimize duplication of pipeline logic across projects; Maximize reusability of pipeline components; Minimize complexity of pipeline maintenance; Maximize understanding of task execution model
notes: Covers the conceptual model of Tasks as building blocks with inputs/outputs, steps as sequential commands, and the pod/container execution model. This is architectural understanding, not tool-specific implementation.

job_statement: When I am creating a Task definition, I want to understand the Task specification structure and required fields, so I can correctly define my pipeline tasks
parent_job: When I am designing a CI/CD workflow, I want to understand how to structure reusable units of work, so I can create maintainable and composable pipeline components
desired_outcomes: Minimize errors in Task YAML syntax; Minimize time spent looking up Task specification fields; Maximize correctness of Task definitions
notes: Specific to understanding the Task YAML structure (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec). The apply-manifests example provides concrete reference material for task authoring.

job_statement: When I need to control pipeline execution flow based on conditions, I want to understand how to guard task execution, so I can implement conditional logic in my pipelines
related_jobs: Handle pipeline failure scenarios; Implement finally tasks
desired_outcomes: Minimize unnecessary task executions in pipelines; Maximize control over pipeline execution paths; Minimize complexity of conditional pipeline logic; Maximize reliability of conditional task execution
notes: Covers the conceptual model of when expressions with input/operator/values components, evaluation timing, and use cases (checking results, file changes, image existence, workspace availability).

job_statement: When I need to skip tasks based on parameter values or task results, I want to understand the when expression syntax and operators, so I can write correct conditional expressions
parent_job: When I need to control pipeline execution flow based on conditions, I want to understand how to guard task execution, so I can implement conditional logic in my pipelines
desired_outcomes: Minimize syntax errors in when expressions; Minimize time spent debugging conditional logic; Maximize understanding of in/notin operators; Maximize correct use of parameters and results in conditions
notes: Specific to the syntax of when expressions including input/operator/values fields and the detailed PipelineRun example showing various condition patterns.

job_statement: When designing a CI/CD pipeline, I want to understand how to ensure cleanup and notification tasks always run, so I can maintain system hygiene and provide consistent feedback regardless of pipeline success or failure
related_jobs: Understanding pipeline execution flow; Understanding task dependencies
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to ensure cleanup operations complete; Minimize the likelihood that resources are left in an inconsistent state; Minimize the uncertainty about whether notification tasks will execute
notes: This is a learning/reference job focused on understanding the finally tasks concept. The section explains that finally tasks run in parallel after all other pipeline tasks finish, regardless of success or failure. This is a stable, outcome-focused goal applicable across different CI/CD tools.

job_statement: When implementing cleanup operations in OpenShift Pipelines, I want to configure finally tasks that consume results from earlier tasks, so I can perform context-aware cleanup and validation
parent_job: When designing a CI/CD pipeline, I want to understand how to ensure cleanup and notification tasks always run, so I can maintain system hygiene and provide consistent feedback regardless of pipeline success or failure
prerequisites: Understanding of OpenShift Pipelines task concept; Understanding of YAML syntax
related_jobs: Defining pipeline workspaces; Referencing task results
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to implement finally tasks; Minimize the complexity of finally task configuration; Minimize the likelihood of cleanup tasks failing
notes: This is a user_story because it's specific to OpenShift Pipelines implementation using the finally field and Tekton syntax. The example shows the clone-cleanup-workspace pipeline with cleanup and check-git-commit finally tasks.

job_statement: When learning CI/CD automation, I want to understand how task definitions are instantiated and executed with specific parameters, so I can control the execution of individual build steps
related_jobs: Understanding task definitions; Understanding pipeline execution
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to understand task execution lifecycle; Minimize the uncertainty about how tasks are started and monitored; Minimize the confusion between task definitions and task instances
notes: This is a learning job focused on understanding the concept of instantiating tasks with specific inputs/outputs. The section explains TaskRun as the instantiation mechanism, which is a stable concept across CI/CD systems even though the implementation is Tekton-specific.

job_statement: When executing a task in OpenShift Pipelines, I want to create a TaskRun resource with the required workspace and parameters, so I can run the task with my specific configuration
parent_job: When learning CI/CD automation, I want to understand how task definitions are instantiated and executed with specific parameters, so I can control the execution of individual build steps
prerequisites: Task definition exists; Workspace configuration is available
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to start a task execution; Minimize the errors in TaskRun configuration; Minimize the complexity of workspace binding
notes: This is a user_story specific to OpenShift Pipelines/Tekton. The example shows the apply-manifests-taskrun with taskRef, workspaces, and serviceAccountName fields. Tool-specific implementation details make this a user_story rather than a main_job.

job_statement: When building CI/CD automation, I want to understand how to compose multiple tasks into an ordered workflow, so I can automate complex build, test, and deployment processes
related_jobs: Understanding task composition; Understanding workflow orchestration
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to design multi-step workflows; Minimize the complexity of task dependencies; Minimize the likelihood of incorrect execution order; Maximize the reusability of workflow components
notes: This is a core learning job about understanding pipeline composition - a stable, outcome-focused concept applicable across CI/CD systems. The section explains how pipelines arrange tasks in execution order to construct complex workflows.

job_statement: When defining a pipeline in OpenShift Pipelines, I want to specify tasks with workspaces, parameters, and execution order using runAfter, so I can create a build-and-deploy workflow
parent_job: When building CI/CD automation, I want to understand how to compose multiple tasks into an ordered workflow, so I can automate complex build, test, and deployment processes
prerequisites: Understanding of YAML syntax; Tasks are available in cluster or namespace
related_jobs: Configuring cluster task resolvers; Defining pipeline parameters; Sharing workspaces between tasks
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to define a pipeline; Minimize the errors in task sequencing; Minimize the complexity of parameter passing; Minimize the setup required for workspace sharing
notes: This is a user_story specific to OpenShift Pipelines/Tekton implementation. The example shows the build-and-deploy pipeline with Tekton-specific fields like taskRef with cluster resolver, runAfter for sequencing, and workspace/param definitions.

job_statement: When executing CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how to instantiate a pipeline definition with specific parameters and credentials for a particular scenario, so I can run my build and deployment process
related_jobs: Understanding pipeline parameterization; Understanding workflow execution lifecycle
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to trigger a workflow execution; Minimize the uncertainty about how to provide runtime parameters; Minimize the complexity of binding workspaces and credentials; Minimize the time it takes to monitor execution progress
notes: This is a core learning job about understanding how to execute pipeline definitions with specific runtime values - a stable concept across CI/CD systems. The section explains PipelineRun as the binding mechanism for pipelines, workspaces, credentials, and parameters.

job_statement: When running a pipeline in OpenShift Pipelines, I want to create a PipelineRun resource with parameter values and workspace volume claims, so I can execute my build-and-deploy workflow for a specific application
parent_job: When executing CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how to instantiate a pipeline definition with specific parameters and credentials for a particular scenario, so I can run my build and deployment process
prerequisites: Pipeline definition exists; Storage class is available for volume claim
related_jobs: Configuring volumeClaimTemplate; Monitoring pipeline run status; Reviewing task run logs
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to start a pipeline execution; Minimize the errors in parameter configuration; Minimize the complexity of workspace provisioning; Minimize the time it takes to identify execution failures
notes: This is a user_story specific to OpenShift Pipelines/Tekton. The example shows the build-deploy-api-pipelinerun with Tekton-specific fields like pipelineRef, volumeClaimTemplate, and the status field for progress tracking.

job_statement: When I need to enforce security or runtime requirements across pipeline executions, I want to understand how to configure pod-level settings, so I can ensure consistent security posture and compliance for all task pods
related_jobs: Understand workspaces for managing shared storage; Configure security contexts in Kubernetes
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to enforce security policies across all pipeline pods; Minimize the likelihood of security violations in task execution; Increase the consistency of runtime configuration across tasks; Minimize the effort required to apply security settings to multiple tasks
notes: Pod templates allow setting parameters like securityContext, schedulerName for all pods in PipelineRun or TaskRun. Common use case is running as non-root user.

job_statement: When I need to run tasks as a specific user or with custom scheduler settings, I want to apply pod template configurations to pipeline runs, so I can meet organizational security or scheduling requirements
parent_job: When I need to enforce security or runtime requirements across pipeline executions, I want to understand how to configure pod-level settings, so I can ensure consistent security posture and compliance for all task pods
prerequisites: Understanding of Kubernetes Pod specifications; Access to PipelineRun or TaskRun definitions
related_jobs: Configure security contexts; Use custom schedulers
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to apply security settings to pipeline runs; Increase the flexibility of pod configuration options; Minimize the risk of running tasks with inappropriate permissions
notes: Examples show runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 1001, and schedulerName: volcano. Different spec locations for PipelineRun (taskRunTemplate.podTemplate) vs TaskRun (podTemplate).

job_statement: When I need to share data between pipeline tasks or provide runtime storage, I want to understand how to declare and configure workspaces, so I can create reusable tasks that work across different environments without hardcoding storage locations
related_jobs: Design reusable tasks; Configure persistent storage in Kubernetes; Share credentials across tasks
desired_outcomes: Increase the reusability of task definitions across different environments; Minimize the coupling between task logic and storage implementation; Minimize the time to share data between sequential or parallel tasks; Increase the flexibility of storage provisioning at runtime; Minimize the complexity of managing task inputs and outputs
notes: Workspaces separate volume declaration from runtime storage. Recommended over PipelineResource CRs. Support multiple backing types: ConfigMap, Secret, PVC, volumeClaimTemplate, emptyDir. Use cases include: storing inputs/outputs, sharing data, mounting credentials/configs, caching build artifacts.

job_statement: When I am building a multi-task pipeline that needs shared storage, I want to declare a workspace in the pipeline and map it to tasks, so I can pass data from one task to another without managing storage directly
parent_job: When I need to share data between pipeline tasks or provide runtime storage, I want to understand how to declare and configure workspaces, so I can create reusable tasks that work across different environments without hardcoding storage locations
prerequisites: Understanding of pipeline and task structure; Knowledge of workspace use cases
related_jobs: Create volumeClaimTemplates for dynamic provisioning; Mount secrets and configmaps as workspaces
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to enable data sharing between tasks; Increase the clarity of data flow in pipeline definitions; Minimize the risk of storage configuration errors
notes: Example shows shared-workspace declared at pipeline level and mapped to tasks (build-image, apply-manifests). PipelineRun provides storage via volumeClaimTemplate.

job_statement: When I need to reuse common step logic across multiple tasks, I want to understand how to define and reference step actions, so I can avoid duplicating step definitions and maintain consistency across task implementations
related_jobs: Design reusable tasks; Use resolvers to reference external resources; Parameterize task definitions
desired_outcomes: Minimize the duplication of step definitions across tasks; Increase the consistency of common actions across pipelines; Minimize the effort required to update shared step logic; Increase the reusability of action definitions across teams; Minimize the maintenance burden for common operations
notes: StepAction CR contains reusable action definitions. Can be referenced from steps in tasks. Supports parameters and results. Does not include workspace definitions (expects task to provide). Security note: parameter values cannot be used directly in scripts, must use env variables.

job_statement: When I want to share a step implementation across tasks or reference external step definitions, I want to create a StepAction resource with parameters and results, so I can invoke the same action from multiple tasks without code duplication
parent_job: When I need to reuse common step logic across multiple tasks, I want to understand how to define and reference step actions, so I can avoid duplicating step definitions and maintain consistency across task implementations
prerequisites: Understanding of task and step structure; Knowledge of parameter and result passing
related_jobs: Use resolvers for external step actions; Define environment variables for parameters
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to implement common steps in new tasks; Increase the security of parameter handling in scripts; Minimize the risk of inconsistent action implementations
notes: Example shows apply-manifests-action referenced from task step using ref.name. Parameters passed from task to step action. Results automatically become step results.

job_statement: When I need to automate pipeline execution in response to external events, I want to understand how triggers capture and process events to instantiate pipeline runs, so I can create event-driven CI/CD workflows without manual intervention
related_jobs: Configure webhooks in source repositories; Design pipeline automation strategies; Implement event-driven architectures
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time between code changes and pipeline execution; Minimize the manual effort required to start pipeline runs; Increase the responsiveness of CI/CD workflows to external events; Minimize the coupling between event sources and pipeline definitions; Increase the automation level of deployment processes
notes: Triggers create comprehensive event-driven CI/CD system. Main components: TriggerBinding (extract event payload), TriggerTemplate (create resources), Trigger (combine binding/template/interceptors), EventListener (HTTP endpoint). Interceptors filter/verify events. Supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Webhook, CEL interceptors.

job_statement: When I receive a Git push event, I want to extract repository information and automatically create a pipeline run with the correct parameters, so I can deploy the latest changes without manual pipeline triggering
parent_job: When I need to automate pipeline execution in response to external events, I want to understand how triggers capture and process events to instantiate pipeline runs, so I can create event-driven CI/CD workflows without manual intervention
prerequisites: Understanding of TriggerBinding and TriggerTemplate; Webhook configured in Git repository; EventListener deployed and accessible
related_jobs: Configure GitHub interceptors for event verification; Define parameter extraction from event payloads; Create pipeline run templates
desired_outcomes: Minimize the delay between push and pipeline execution; Increase the accuracy of parameter extraction from events; Minimize the configuration complexity of event-driven pipelines
notes: Example shows vote-app trigger: TriggerBinding extracts git-repo-url, git-repo-name, git-revision from body. TriggerTemplate creates PipelineRun with extracted params. Trigger combines them with GitHub interceptor for push events. EventListener provides HTTP endpoint.
